quote: you guys would just need to have a form of taxable income and a credit score of six fifty or higher. Is that the case for you guys?
stewart_read: The rep blended Ion's requirement with tax-incentive eligibility in one breath, which is exactly the ambiguity the customer immediately caught.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be intentional shorthand the rep normally gets away with, but the customer's direct challenge shows it failed here.
coaching_implication: Separate the two clauses explicitly: 'To qualify for OUR program you need X; that's different from the federal tax credit eligibility.'

quote: Is that for me to qualify with you guys or to qualify with the tax and incentives?
stewart_read: This is a trust/clarity objection stalling the qualifier section; rep should have cleanly restated the distinction rather than a garbled 'that's qualify me.'
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have understood but simply communicated poorly under a rambling call style rather than lacking the knowledge.
coaching_implication: Practice a one-line clean split of program-qualifier vs tax-credit-qualifier so this doesn't stall the section.

quote: Not for the incentives for you guys. No. That's what you're asking me for.
stewart_read: Second touch on the same unresolved confusion — customer is now doing the rep's clarifying work for him.
coaching_implication: If the customer has to restate the distinction twice, the rep has lost control of the qualifier beat; needs a scripted fallback line.

stewart_read: The bill amount, the single most important anchor in the whole call, was let go with a one-word acceptance and no pivot to a verbal estimate or alternate capture path.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be deferring bill capture to the design/specialist stage deliberately, but the schema treats capture as necessary before that handoff and there is no signal here that this was a plan rather than a drop.
coaching_implication: When customer doesn't know the exact number, ask for a ballpark or last winter/summer high bill instead of moving straight past it.

stewart_read: Customer explicitly declines to send a bill and the rep does not pivot to a verbal read-back or utility-website walk-through — he just accepts it and moves to a design based on square footage alone.
coaching_implication: This is the exact trigger the elderly_low_tech_protocol/landline_protocol alternative paths are built for — pivot within 2 minutes to verbal readback instead of dropping the ask.

stewart_read: Customer's stated interest is backup power during outages — a Powerwall/battery cross-sell signal — and the rep briefly acknowledges it ('backup options') but never returns to it or ties it to next steps.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be leaving battery discussion for the closer intentionally, consistent with setter scope discipline.
coaching_implication: Even under scope discipline, the rep should flag the backup interest explicitly for the handoff so the closer leads with Powerwall framing.

quote: we'll just kinda get this design started here for you. We'll kinda base it off of Yeah. Yeah. Just kinda 756 square feet.
stewart_read: The call ends with a design being built off square footage alone (no bill, no usage history) and a vague future callback — no button-up elements were run at all.
coaching_implication: Even without a firm appointment, rep should lock a specific day/time for the follow-up call rather than 'I'll give you another call here.'
